title: The Stark Munro Letters
summary: Presented as a genuine correspondence edited by one Herbert Swanborough, this epistolary novel consists of twelve letters written by young Dr. J. Stark Munro to his American friend during 1881-1884, recounting the early struggles of a newly qualified physician trying to establish himself in practice. The narrative centers on Munro's turbulent partnership with James Cullingworth, a brilliant, eccentric, and volatile former fellow-student whose inventive genius, wild temper, and unorthodox medical theories repeatedly draw Munro into chaotic ventures, from a shared practice to dubious business schemes and inventions like a naval magnet device. Alongside the comic and adventurous escapades with Cullingworth, the letters trace Munro's inner life: his religious doubts and rejection of orthodox faith, his financial hardships, his romantic disappointments, and his gradual maturing sense of professional and personal purpose. Written in a warm, reflective, autobiographical voice drawing heavily on Doyle's own early medical career, the book blends humor, philosophical musing, and adventure. A framing note reveals the fate of Munro and his family, closing the correspondence with poignant finality.
